synopsis: ISO 18497-2:2024 covers agricultural obstacle-protection systems, and the booklet treats the ISO 18497 family as a close cousin of heavy off-road collision mitigation and the nearest published off-road precedent for standardized perception test objects [f7188, f7190, f451]. Parts 1–4 were published in July 2024; the planning chapter reports that Parts 1, 2 and 4 replaced ISO 18497:2018 [f7187, f9763]. Part 2 starts from the premise that detection cannot work perfectly under all conditions and identifies four failure categories: failure to detect, late detection, incorrect classification and localization error [f1396, f1712]. The booklet recommends structuring the scenario catalogue around these categories alongside ISO 21815-3 risk areas, and considers the categories relevant to architectures that limit what perception must prove [f1605, f15289, f443]. Although the family includes verification methods and test objects, the review did not find a minimum-method table in Parts 1, 2 and 4; the EN adoption of Part 2 also includes an Annex ZA linking it to the Machinery Directive [f450, f9765, f1397].
